headline: Healthcare Holds as Semis and Industrials Buckle Under Geopolitical Pressure
body_html:
Wednesday's mid-session picture is decidedly lopsided: 160 stocks in our 544-name universe are trading higher against 378 in the red, with selling pressure concentrated in semiconductors, homebuilders, and industrials. A hotter-than-expected September consumer-price reading — driven by costlier gasoline and firmer core inflation — rattled rate-sensitive corners of the market at the open and the damage has yet to fully reverse.

Healthcare is the clear defensive anchor, gaining roughly 0.7% as a sector and supplying four of the day's six top gainers. Eli Lilly and AstraZeneca each rose nearly 4%, while NeoGenomics and argenx added more than 3%. GSK rounds out pharma's strong showing. On the opposite end, semiconductors are off more than 3% as a group, with equipment and chip-software names bearing the brunt. Enphase Energy leads all decliners, down more than 8%, dragging the solar cohort lower alongside a broad Industrials retreat that has also claimed GE Vernova and Forgent Power Solutions, each off roughly 7%.

Into the close, traders will watch whether the geopolitical risk premium tied to Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure continues to lift energy-price expectations — a dynamic that could either reinforce inflation fears or pivot flows toward domestic energy names. The September CPI print will remain the macro anchor for the remainder of the session.

briefs.headline: September CPI Comes in Hot, Rattling Rate Expectations
briefs.body: Consumer prices accelerated in September, lifted by higher gasoline costs and a firmer core reading, according to fresh government data. The report has rekindled debate over how much further the Federal Reserve has to go, casting a shadow over rate-sensitive sectors including homebuilders, which are off nearly 3% midday.

briefs.headline: Houthi Strike on Aramco HQ Sends Shockwaves Through Gulf Markets
briefs.body: Saudi stocks were the hardest hit across Gulf markets after Houthi militants struck the Saudi Aramco headquarters, with sources describing extensive structural damage. The group subsequently vowed additional attacks on Saudi airports and oil infrastructure, injecting a fresh layer of geopolitical risk into energy markets midweek.

briefs.headline: Shipping Lane Anxiety Rises After Vessel Sunk Near Hormuz
briefs.body: A container ship was struck by a projectile and sank near the Strait of Hormuz, sources told Reuters, adding to a string of maritime incidents in the region. The development, alongside reports of drone activity off southern Iran injuring three fishermen, is keeping traders alert to potential supply-chain disruptions through one of the world's most critical chokepoints.

briefs.headline: Eli Lilly and AstraZeneca Lead Pharma's Defensive Rally
briefs.body: Both Eli Lilly and AstraZeneca climbed just under 4% in mid-session trading, making them the joint top gainers in our universe today. The moves underscore a flight toward large-cap pharmaceuticals as investors seek shelter from macro headwinds and geopolitical uncertainty dominating Wednesday's tape.

briefs.headline: Power-Equipment Names Hit Hard as Industrials Slide
briefs.body: GE Vernova fell more than 7% and Forgent Power Solutions dropped over 7% midday, two of the steepest declines within a broader industrials sector that is off roughly 1.4% as a group. The selloff in power-infrastructure names reflects a mix of macro rate concerns and sector-specific sentiment souring on prior momentum trades.

briefs.headline: Iran's Central Bank Pushes Back on Economic-Collapse Talk
briefs.body: Iran's central bank governor publicly rejected claims that the country's economy is on the verge of collapse amid an ongoing U.S. blockade, seeking to project stability. The statement comes as regional tensions escalate on multiple fronts, with the Hormuz shipping incident and continued Houthi activity keeping Middle East risk elevated for market participants.
